Approaches herein provide a torch handle including a pneumatically controlled jaw operable to engage an electrode. In one approach, a system is provided for distributing gas within the torch handle, the system including a pneumatic cylinder within a main housing of the torch handle. The pneumatic cylinder is coupled to a shaft for actuating a first member of a jaw relative to a second member of the jaw. The system further includes a gas passageway through the main housing, the gas passageway extending to an exit orifice disposed within the second member. A flow controller is operable to direct a flow of a gas to either the pneumatic cylinder or the gas passageway. In one approach, the first member is actuated towards the second member when the gas is directed through the gas passageway, and actuated away from the second member when the gas is directed to the pneumatic cylinder.

outputs.L1: The approaches described herein provide a torch handle comprising a pneumatically controlled jaw operable to engage an electrode. In one approach, a system for distributing gas within the torch handle includes a pneumatic cylinder positioned within a main housing of the torch handle. The pneumatic cylinder is coupled to a shaft configured to actuate a first member of the jaw relative to a second member of the jaw. The system further includes a gas passageway extending through the main housing to an exit orifice disposed within the second member. A flow controller is operable to direct a flow of gas to either the pneumatic cylinder or the gas passageway. In one approach, the first member is actuated toward the second member when the gas is directed through the gas passageway and is actuated away from the second member when the gas is directed to the pneumatic cylinder.
outputs.L2: The disclosed implementations concern a torch handle having a pneumatically operated jaw configured to grip an electrode. In one implementation, the torch handle includes a gas-distribution system with a pneumatic cylinder positioned inside the handle’s main housing. The cylinder is connected to a shaft that moves a first jaw component relative to a second jaw component. A gas channel also passes through the main housing and terminates at an outlet opening located in the second jaw component. A flow-control device selectively routes gas either to the pneumatic cylinder or through the gas channel. When gas is sent through the channel, the first jaw component moves toward the second component; when gas is supplied to the pneumatic cylinder, the first component moves away from the second component.
outputs.L3:
The torch handle incorporates a pneumatically controlled jaw assembly configured to engage and retain an electrode. A pneumatic cylinder is positioned within the main housing of the torch handle and is mechanically coupled to a shaft. The shaft actuates a first jaw member relative to a second jaw member, thereby opening or closing the jaw assembly.

A gas passageway extends through the main housing and terminates at an exit orifice located within the second jaw member. A flow controller selectively directs a supply of gas either to the pneumatic cylinder or through the gas passageway. When gas is directed through the passageway toward the exit orifice, the first jaw member moves toward the second jaw member to engage the electrode. Conversely, when gas is directed to the pneumatic cylinder, the cylinder actuates the shaft to move the first jaw member away from the second jaw member, releasing the electrode.
outputs.L4:
The torch handle includes a pneumatically actuated jaw assembly configured to selectively engage and retain an electrode. An internal pneumatic cylinder and movable shaft are coupled to the jaw so that movement of the shaft changes the jaw between open and closed positions. The handle also defines a gas passageway that carries pressurized gas through the torch and distributes the gas to the appropriate operating components.

A flow controller selectively directs the incoming gas along different flow paths. When gas is directed through the passageway associated with closing the jaw, pneumatic pressure causes the jaw to move into engagement with the electrode, thereby securing the electrode in place. When the flow controller instead routes gas to the pneumatic cylinder, the resulting movement of the cylinder and shaft opens the jaw and releases the electrode.

Accordingly, the same gas supply can support both gas distribution through the torch and pneumatic operation of the electrode-retaining mechanism. By controlling the path of the gas, an operator can engage or disengage the electrode without relying on a separate mechanical actuation system.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for a torch handle with a pneumatically controlled jaw that grips an electrode and selectively routes gas to either a pneumatic cylinder or an outlet near the jaw.
counterfactuals.output: A torch handle includes a body defining a gas inlet, a gas outlet positioned adjacent an electrode-receiving jaw, and a pneumatic passage communicating with a cylinder. The cylinder is operatively coupled to the jaw to move the jaw between an electrode-gripping position and an electrode-release position. A valve assembly selectively directs pressurized gas received through the gas inlet to either the pneumatic passage, thereby actuating the cylinder and jaw, or the gas outlet, thereby delivering a gas flow near an electrode retained by the jaw. The valve assembly may inhibit gas delivery to the outlet during actuation of the cylinder and may vent the cylinder to permit return movement of the jaw. The integrated arrangement enables pneumatic electrode clamping and localized gas delivery through a common gas supply within the torch handle.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an invention in formal patent language involving a torch handle, an electrode-engaging jaw, a pneumatic actuator, a gas passageway, and a flow controller.
counterfactuals.output:
**Title: Pneumatically Actuated Torch Electrode Retention and Gas-Flow Control Assembly**

An apparatus for use with a torch comprises an elongate torch handle defining an internal cavity and having a distal end configured to receive an electrode. An electrode-engaging jaw is disposed adjacent the distal end of the torch handle and is movable between an open position, in which insertion or removal of the electrode is permitted, and a closed position, in which the electrode is releasably retained in an operative position.

A pneumatic actuator is operatively coupled to the electrode-engaging jaw and is configured, upon application of pressurized gas, to move the electrode-engaging jaw between the open and closed positions. A gas passageway extends through at least a portion of the torch handle and is in fluid communication with the pneumatic actuator and a gas inlet. A flow controller is disposed in fluid communication with the gas passageway and is selectively operable to regulate a flow of gas through the gas passageway. The flow controller may be configured to direct the pressurized gas to the pneumatic actuator, to a torch gas outlet surrounding or adjacent the electrode, or to both.

In certain embodiments, the flow controller comprises a valve responsive to manual actuation, an electrical control signal, or a detected operating condition of the torch. The flow controller may coordinate movement of the electrode-engaging jaw with delivery of a shielding, cutting, or plasma-forming gas. A biasing member may urge the jaw toward a predetermined position in the absence of pneumatic pressure, thereby permitting secure electrode retention or fail-safe electrode release.

**Representative Independent Claim**

1. A torch assembly comprising:  
   a torch handle having a distal electrode-receiving portion;  
   an electrode-engaging jaw supported by the torch handle and movable between an open position and an electrode-retaining position;  
   a pneumatic actuator operatively connected to the electrode-engaging jaw and configured to move the electrode-engaging jaw in response to pneumatic pressure;  
   a gas passageway extending through the torch handle and fluidly coupled to the pneumatic actuator; and  
   a flow controller in fluid communication with the gas passageway, the flow controller being selectively operable to regulate delivery of pressurized gas through the gas passageway to control actuation of the electrode-engaging jaw.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a concise technical summary of a welding torch handle in which gas flow controls the opening and closing of an electrode clamp.
counterfactuals.output: A welding torch handle integrates the shielding-gas passage with a pressure-actuated electrode clamp. When gas is admitted, pressure drives an internal piston or diaphragm linked to the clamping mechanism, moving the jaws to release or secure the electrode. Shutting off or venting the gas allows a return spring to move the clamp to its opposite position. This arrangement coordinates electrode retention with gas flow, reduces manual operations, and provides a compact, sealed control mechanism within the handle.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a patent abstract for a system that uses a pneumatic cylinder and shaft to move one jaw member relative to another, while also distributing gas through an exit orifice in the fixed jaw member.
counterfactuals.output: A jaw assembly includes a fixed jaw member, a movable jaw member, and a pneumatic actuator configured to move the movable jaw member relative to the fixed jaw member. The pneumatic actuator includes a cylinder and a shaft operatively coupled to the movable jaw member. Pressurized gas supplied to the cylinder drives the shaft between retracted and extended positions to selectively open or close the jaw assembly. A gas-distribution passage fluidly couples a gas source to an exit orifice formed in the fixed jaw member, enabling gas to be discharged adjacent to a workpiece engaged by the jaw members. The gas used for actuation and the gas supplied to the exit orifice may originate from a common source and may be independently controlled. The assembly thereby provides pneumatic jaw movement and localized gas delivery in an integrated structure.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Explain, using “in one approach” patent phrasing, how gas can be selectively directed within a torch handle so that one flow path closes a jaw and another opens it.
counterfactuals.output: In one approach, a torch handle includes a gas-routing valve selectively movable between first and second operating states. In the first state, the valve fluidly couples a pressurized-gas inlet to a first passage communicating with a closing chamber of a jaw actuator, thereby urging a movable jaw toward a closed position. In the second state, the valve couples the inlet to a second passage communicating with an opening chamber of the actuator, thereby urging the movable jaw toward an open position. The chamber not being pressurized may be vented through the valve or a separate exhaust passage. A trigger, lever, or other user-operated control can shift the valve between the states, allowing gas supplied to the handle to selectively close or open the jaw.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
